MINOR: `sys.stdout.reconfigure` mutates process-global stream state inside a per-record helper; once any gate record reconfigures stdout, all subsequent output in the process (other gates, tooling, test capture) inherits `errors="replace"`, silently masking encoding defects elsewhere. Scope the reconfiguration to the specific print (e.g., wrap the rendered text) instead of the global stream, or document it as a process-wide invariant.

The blanket `except Exception: pass` around `reconfigure` gives no observability when reconfiguration fails; a debug-level log or comment on why failure is safe would keep the fail-open behavior auditable per ENGINEERING_OPERATING_STANDARD observability expectations.
NIT: The `try/except` is nested inside an existing `try`; hoisting the reconfigure into the module's import/startup path would make the encoding policy a single explicit decision rather than a per-call side effect.
SUMMARY: The delta is a one-line defensive encoding fix in `gate_decisions.py`; it does not affect residency ACs, which remain evidenced at HEAD.
Only concern is the global, silently-failing `stdout.reconfigure` side effect — low risk, worth scoping or documenting rather than blocking.
